title: Session Tab Reversal
real_world_story: When a browser user switches display modes between Left-to-Right (LTR) and Right-to-Left (RTL), or triggers an 'Invert Tab Order' session rearrangement, the underlying tab list must be reversed in-place. The tab nodes' next pointers must be inverted directly in memory without allocating auxiliary list nodes.
problem_statement: Given a singly linked list representing the sequence of N open browser tab IDs from leftmost to rightmost, reverse the linked list in-place by updating the node pointers. Output the tab IDs in the reversed order. If the list is empty (N = 0), print 'EMPTY'.
task: Reverse the given singly linked list of tab IDs and print the resulting sequence from new head to tail.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of open tabs.
The second line contains N space-separated integers representing the tab IDs from left to right. If N = 0, this line is empty or omitted.
output_format: Print the space-separated tab IDs in reversed order. If N = 0, print EMPTY.

examples.explanation: The linked list 10 -> 20 -> 30 -> 40 -> 50 is reversed in-place to 50 -> 40 -> 30 -> 20 -> 10.
A single-element list remains unchanged when reversed.
For 0 tabs, the output is EMPTY.

real_world_takeaway: In-place pointer reversal avoids memory overhead and garbage collection pauses when restructuring large linear UI session state.
